title.en: Describe the institutional structure of rural credit

say.en: A farmer sows in June but sells his crop only in November. For five months he must buy seeds, fertiliser and food. Where does the money come from, and at what price? In this lesson: Explain why farmers need credit.
Describe the institutional structure of rural credit.
Explain micro-credit through SHGs.

body.en: Because of the long gap between sowing and harvest, farmers borrow for seeds, fertilisers and implements, and also for family needs such as marriages and illness. Earlier, moneylenders and traders charged very high interest and manipulated accounts, trapping farmers in debt. After the nationalisation of banks in 1969, India adopted social banking and a multi-agency approach. NABARD (1982) is the apex body coordinating *rural* financing through commercial banks, regional rural banks (RRBs), cooperatives and land development banks.
body.kn: ಬಿತ್ತನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕೊಯ್ಲಿನ ನಡುವೆ ದೀರ್ಘ ಅವಧಿ ಇರುವುದರಿಂದ ರೈತರಿಗೆ ಸಾಲ ಬೇಕು. ಲೇವಾದೇವಿಗಾರರು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಬಡ್ಡಿ ವಿಧಿಸಿ ಸಾಲದ ಬಲೆಗೆ ಸಿಲುಕಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದರು. 1969 ರ ನಂತರ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳು ಹಳ್ಳಿಗಳಿಗೆ ವಿಸ್ತರಿಸಿದವು; 1982 ರಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಾಪಿತವಾದ ನಬಾರ್ಡ್ ಗ್ರಾಮೀಣ ಹಣಕಾಸನ್ನು ಸಂಯೋಜಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: The teacher draws the institutional structure of rural credit with NABARD at the top, adds SHGs and moneylenders, and compares the cost of a loan.

say.en: At the top is NABARD, the apex body for rural finance, set up in 1982.
Under it, four kinds of formal lenders: commercial banks, regional rural banks, cooperatives and land development banks.
They lend to farmers. Self-help groups give small loans from pooled savings. The moneylender is still there, charging high interest.
Why it matters: ten thousand rupees for three years at thirty-six percent becomes over twenty-five thousand; at a bank's seven percent it is about twelve thousand two hundred.

body.en: *Self-help groups* (SHGs) encourage thrift: each member saves a small amount regularly, and the pooled money is lent to members at reasonable interest. With SHG-bank linkage, banks also lend to SHGs. This micro-credit has helped poor women in particular, though formal credit is still not enough and loan recovery has been a problem for rural banks.
body.kn: ಸ್ವಸಹಾಯ ಗುಂಪುಗಳು ಸದಸ್ಯರಿಂದ ಸಣ್ಣ ಉಳಿತಾಯ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ ಅದರಿಂದ ಸಾಲ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳೂ ಈ ಗುಂಪುಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಾಲ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ. ಈ ಕಿರುಸಾಲ ವಿಶೇಷವಾಗಿ ಬಡ ಮಹಿಳೆಯರಿಗೆ ಸಹಾಯಕ.

problem.en: A farmer borrows ₹10,000 for 3 years, either from a moneylender at 36% a year or from a bank at 7% a year (interest compounded yearly, nothing repaid). Compare the amounts owed.

answer.en: About ₹25,155 to the moneylender against about ₹12,250 to the bank

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A farmer borrows ₹10,000 for 3 years, either from a moneylender at 36% a year or from a bank at 7% a year (interest compounded yearly, nothing repaid). Compare the amounts owed.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A farmer borrows 10,000 rupees for 3 years, either from a moneylender at 36 percent a year or from a bank at 7 percent a year (interest compounded yearly, nothing repaid). Compare the amounts owed.
Moneylender: 10,000 times 1.36 cubed equals 10,000 times 2.515456 equals 25,154.56 rupees.
Bank: 10,000 times 1.07 cubed equals 10,000 times 1.225043 equals 12,250.43 rupees.
Extra cost of the moneylender equals 25,154.56 minus 12,250.43 equals 12,904.13 rupees.
So the answer is About 25,155 rupees to the moneylender against about 12,250 rupees to the bank.
